feedback: The candidate changes one variable: kd 0.4 to 0.5, with kp 7.0, geometry, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05 and last_direction unchanged from iteration 3. The rationale matches the evidence. Iteration 3 (kp 7.0, kd 0.4) was the best so far at 82.74, but every trial still went off track. Its oval steering_oscillation was 0.25, above the 0.2 concern level, while the s-bend (0.12) and slalom (0.13) were low. Its max_error of 0.061 to 0.065 sat just over the 0.06 limit, and line losses were down to 1 per run on the s-bend and slalom. The planned response to oscillation above about 0.2 is to raise kd before cutting kp, and cutting kp now would weaken the edge response that is holding max_error near 0.06. Nothing here states how this candidate will perform. After the race, use the telemetry as follows. If oval steering_oscillation falls below about 0.2 while max_error stays near 0.06 or lower, keep kd 0.5 and test a wider array (x = ±0.040 m, 16 mm sensors) with kp near 8. If oscillation stays above 0.2 with kd 0.5, try kd 0.6 before reducing kp. If max_error is still at or above 0.06 with oscillation low, widen the array as above. If line_loss_events stay at 1 per run at the same bend entries, test line_loss search_left or search_right, choosing the side the failing bends favour. If progress is still below 1 with max_error under 0.06, raise base_speed toward 1.6. Approve now: this is the best-supported next step, it is a small change from the best raced design, and a race is the only way to learn more with 7 iterations left.
